statement.text:
A Schmidt (p, q)-group is a finite non-nilpotent group all of whose proper
subgroups are nilpotent and whose Sylow p-subgroup is normal. The N -critical graph
ΓN c (G) of a finite group G is a directed graph on the vertex set of all prime divisors of
|G| in which (p, q) is an edge of ΓN c (G) if and only if G has a Schmidt (p, q)-subgroup.
Suppose that a finite group G is such that G = AB = AC = BC, where A, B, C are
subgroups of G. Is ΓN c (G) = ΓN c (A) ∪ ΓN c (B) ∪ ΓN c (C)? This is true if A, B, C are
soluble.                                                     V. I. Murashka, A. F. Vasil’ev
